V1|updated|run1.question: What does RVISmith fuzz, and what does it target?
V1|updated|run1.answer:
RVISmith is a fuzzer for **compilers**, specifically for **RVV (RISC-V Vector Extension) intrinsics**. The paper says: “our work focuses on detecting compiler bugs for RVV (RISC-V Vector Extension) intrinsics” [DBLP_journals_cacm_WangZKS16 p.2], and “we have proposed an approach of fuzzing compilers for RVV intrinsics” [DBLP_journals_cacm_WangZKS16 p.13].

It targets **the open RISC-V ISA**: “RVV intrinsics are nascent and target the open RISC-V ISA” [DBLP_journals_cacm_WangZKS16 p.2]. More specifically, it “generates well-defined C programs that include various invocation sequences of RVV intrinsics” [DBLP_journals_cacm_WangZKS16 p.2].

V2|updated|run1.answer:
MANTRA is “a framework for automatically generating and validating compliance benchmarks for tool-using LLM agents from procedural manuals and tool schemas” [DBLP_conf_icse_JeonQFFS16 p.14].

It validates “compliance benchmarks” and, more specifically, “trace-level compliance checks” for agent tool-use sequences: “MANTRA does not only verify a final output, but constructs trace-level compliance checks to evaluate sequences of tool calls” [DBLP_conf_icse_JeonQFFS16 p.3]. It also says these checks “specify whether such a trace complies with the sampled document region” and “provide a deterministic evaluation procedure for agent traces” [DBLP_conf_icse_JeonQFFS16 p.4][DBLP_conf_icse_JeonQFFS16 p.5].

based methods can complement each other in the development
and evaluation of AI systems. More broadly, such combinations may help make
AI systems more trustworthy in settings where procedural compliance matters,
including enterprise, regulatory, and safety-critical workflows. At the same time,
MANTRA is not a standalone guarantee of safe or compliant behavior, but rather
one component of a broader assurance process. We hope this work encourages
further research at the interface of machine learning and formal methods for
evaluating increasingly capable LLM agents.
6 Conclusion
We present MANTRA, a framework for automatically generating and validating
compliance benchmarks for tool-using LLM agents from procedural manuals
and tool schemas. By combining LLM-based generation with SMT-based cross-
validation, MANTRA produces high-quality test cases with deterministic trace-

V6|updated|run1.question: What does BLK-Assist propose?
V6|updated|run1.answer:
BLK-Assist proposes “a modular framework for artist-specific fine-tuning of diffusion models using parameter-efficient methods” [DBLP_conf_pldi_Solar-LezamaATBSS07 p.1].

The paper says the system is “implemented as a case study with a single professional artist’s proprietary corpus” and consists of three components: “BLK-Conceptor,” “BLK-Stencil,” and “BLK-Upscale” [DBLP_conf_pldi_Solar-LezamaATBSS07 p.1].

More specifically, it proposes:
- “BLK-Conceptor” for “rapid conceptual sketching, composition, and lighting exploration” [DBLP_conf_pldi_Solar-LezamaATBSS07 p.2]
- “BLK-Stencil” for “transparency-preserving asset generation” [DBLP_conf_pldi_Solar-LezamaATBSS07 p.1]
- “BLK-Upscale” for “high-resolution outputs” [DBLP_conf_pldi_Solar-LezamaATBSS07 p.1]

Overall, the framework aims to provide “a privacy-preserving, consent-based approach to human–AI co-creation that maintains stylistic fidelity to the source corpus” [DBLP_conf_pldi_Solar-LezamaATBSS07 p.1].

V8|updated|run1.question: What does the Advanced Encryption Standard specify?
V8|updated|run1.answer:
The excerpt says the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) “specifies a FIPS-approved cryptographic algorithm that can be used to protect electronic data” [DBLP_journals_sttt_Solar-Lezama13 p.1].

It further explains that AES is “a symmetric block cipher that can encrypt (encipher) and decrypt (decipher) information” [DBLP_journals_sttt_Solar-Lezama13 p.1], and that it “specifies the Rijndael algorithm … a symmetric block cipher that can process data blocks of 128 bits, using cipher keys with lengths of 128, 192, and 256 bits” [DBLP_journals_sttt_Solar-Lezama13 p.9].

So, in short: AES specifies a FIPS-approved symmetric block cipher for protecting electronic data [DBLP_journals_sttt_Solar-Lezama13 p.1].

N5|updated|run1.question: What about sketching?
N5|updated|run1.answer:
The excerpts say sketching is “a new form of localized software synthesis” that uses “partial programs” to let the programmer describe the “desired implementation strategy,” while “leav[ing] the low-level details of the implementation to an automated synthesis procedure” [DBLP_conf_aplas_Solar-Lezama09 p.1].

They also say, more specifically, that “Sketching is a new form of localized program synthesis that allows programmers to express their high-level insights about a problem by writing a sketch—a partial program that encodes the structure of a solution while leaving its low-level details unspecified” [DBLP_conf_aplas_Solar-Lezama09 p.1].

And one excerpt adds that sketching’s benefit is that it lets the system synthesize “an implementation that conforms to a sketch,” while “Sketch resolution” is the step that “synthesizes the details missing in a sketch” [DBLP_conf_pldi_Solar-LezamaRBE05 p.8].

So, in short: sketching is program synthesis from a partial, constrained program sketch rather than a full implementation [DBLP_conf_aplas_Solar-Lezama09 p.1; DBLP_conf_pldi_Solar-LezamaRBE05 p.8].

Armando Solar-Lezama

aims to bridge the gap between a programmer’s high-level insights about

implementation strategy, and leaves the low-level details of the imple-
mentation to an automated synthesis procedure. This paper describes
the sketching approach to program synthesis, including the details of the

unspecified. In addition to the sketch, programmers provide the synthesizer with
either a reference implementation or a set of test routines that the synthesized
code must pass. The Sketch synthesis engine is able to derive the missing details
in the sketch to produce a working implementation that satisfies the correct
